_comment: The curated asset. Everything else in this directory is mechanical; this
file is the part a human has to keep true, and therefore the part that is
worth money. Each entry carries the first-party source it came from so a
buyer can audit the claim rather than trust it.
Scope note that matters more than it looks: this course targets AZURE
OpenAI (see requirements.txt - azure-ai-projects, agent-framework-foundry).
Azure's retirement schedule is not OpenAI's. OpenAI retired gpt-4o from
ChatGPT on 2026-02-13 with no API change; Azure Foundry runs its own
lifecycle. Grading these pins against the wrong platform's calendar is the
single easiest way to publish a confidently wrong drift report.
Also note the course pins models UNVERSIONED ('gpt-4o', not
'gpt-4o-2024-05-13'). Which version a learner actually gets depends on
their Foundry deployment, so severity here reflects the EARLIEST retiring
version a bare pin can resolve to. That is the conservative read and it is
the one an operator planning a migration needs.
2026-08-28 growth pass (worker-008): o3-mini's replacement was corrected
from gpt-5.1 to o4-mini per the commercial (non-Gov) retirement schedule,
which is the table that applies unless a deployment is confirmed on Azure
Government - the Gov schedule this entry previously cited names a
different replacement than the commercial one for the same model/date.
Two Phi models were added (course uses phi-4-mini via Foundry Local) and
a run of Anthropic Claude models were added from Anthropic's own
model-deprecations page, since the MODEL_ID regex in drift_scan.py also
matches claude-* pins - none are pinned in the current course checkout,
but a future lesson easily could reference one and Anthropic runs its own
retirement calendar just as Azure does for OpenAI models. Note for the
next catalog session: several Azure o-series ids (o1, o3, o3-mini,
o4-mini, o1-pro, ...) can never be matched by MODEL_PATTERNS as written -
the regex requires a literal '-' immediately after the 'o' alternative,
which none of those ids have (compare 'o3-mini': o,3,-,m... - the second
character is '3', not '-'). That's a scanner bug, out of this brief's
scope (catalog only), but it means o3-mini/codex-mini entries already in
this file are inert against MODEL_PATTERNS today; flagged here rather
than silently left for someone to discover by confusion. Google's
Gemini deprecation pages and OpenAI's platform.openai.com deprecations
page were both unreachable from this sandbox (egress-proxy blocked); no
dates were guessed, they were skipped.
2026-08-28 growth pass (worker-office/wordsworth008): added 25 more OpenAI-
family entries (o1, o1-pro, o3, o3-deep-research, o3-pro, o4-mini, and the
gpt-5.x/-chat/-codex generation through gpt-5.6-luna/sol/terra), all from
the same Azure Foundry retirement-schedule page as the existing gpt-4o/
gpt-5 entries. Same caveat as the existing scope note applies doubly here:
this is AZURE's retirement schedule for these models, not OpenAI's own
platform.openai.com schedule, which remained unreachable from this sandbox
this pass too (confirmed again, EGRESS_BLOCKED). Skipped entries with
ambiguous multi-version rows this pass could not resolve to one honest
date without guessing: gpt-chat-latest (four Preview rows, two with
retirement dates already in the past relative to each other in a way that
does not resolve to one clear lifecycle) and the gpt-realtime-mini/gpt-
realtime-* family (repeated version+date rows disagreeing by up to nine
months for what the table presents as the same version). Also out of
scope this pass: audio/image/tts/whisper/embedding/transcribe model ids,
kept out because the brief's priority was GPT/o-series text models and
because several of those rows share the same multi-version ambiguity.
Google Gemini: ai.google.dev and cloud.google.com/docs.cloud.google.com
remained EGRESS_BLOCKED (reconfirmed, including the docs.cloud.google.com
redirect target). Checked the google-gemini GitHub org for a first-party
structured deprecation source (cookbook, api-examples, gemini-skills, gemini-
cli, and others) - none carry a deprecation/retirement schedule, only prose
model-name mentions in READMEs. No Gemini entries added; see the ticket for
the full unreachable-source list.

gpt-4o.detail: Azure Foundry lists gpt-4o version 2024-05-13 as Deprecated with a retirement date of 2026-10-01; versions 2024-08-06 and 2024-11-20 run to 2027-04-14. Because this pin carries no version, a deployment on 2024-05-13 stops serving on 2026-10-01 and returns hard errors. Microsoft's listed replacement is gpt-5.1.

gpt-4o-mini.detail: Azure Foundry lists gpt-4o-mini version 2024-07-18 as Deprecated with a retirement date of 2027-04-14. Deprecated means no new deployments and a fixed end date, so this is a scheduled migration rather than an emergency. Microsoft lists no direct replacement; gpt-5.1 is the current GA general-purpose model.

gpt-4.1.detail: Azure Foundry lists gpt-4.1 version 2025-04-14 as Legacy with a retirement date of 2027-04-14. Legacy still accepts new deployments, so this is informational: safe to keep teaching, worth a note that it is not the current default.

gpt-4.1-mini.detail: Azure Foundry lists gpt-4.1-mini version 2025-04-14 as Legacy with a retirement date of 2027-04-14. Still deployable; no action required before 2027.

gpt-4.1-nano.detail: Azure Foundry lists gpt-4.1-nano version 2025-04-14 as Legacy with a retirement date of 2027-04-14.

gpt-5.1.detail: GA on Azure Foundry and the listed replacement target for the retiring gpt-4o line.

o3-mini.detail: Azure Foundry's commercial-cloud retirement schedule lists o3-mini (version 2025-01-31) as Deprecated with a retirement date of 2026-10-01, replacement o4-mini. (A prior version of this entry cited the Azure Government schedule, which lists the same model and date but names gpt-5.1 as the replacement instead - the two clouds' schedules can diverge on replacement even when the retirement date matches. This entry now follows the commercial schedule, since that is what applies unless a deployment is confirmed to be on Azure Government.)
